mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically for three consecutive weeks (-71.4 to -65.4), indicating an ongoing recovery trend in discretionary mobility that should persist and extend over the next four weeks as consumer routines continue to normalize.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved each week from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days, breaking the established upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility falls more than 5 points week-on-week from its current level, reduced access to transit hubs will mechanically suppress trips to retail and recreation venues reachable primarily by public transport, pulling RETAIL_REC down over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -60.6 in t-0w after fluctuating between -63.9 and -60.6
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat over the next 2 weeks despite a TRANSIT drop exceeding 5 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has remained persistently elevated (16-17.4) with little variation, indicating a stable behavioral baseline of increased home-centered time that caps the ceiling for RETAIL_REC recovery, keeping it from rising meaningfully over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed in a narrow 16.0-17.4 band across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises by more than 3 points on average over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above 16.

mechanism_narrative: A joint recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT (both rising together) amplifies RETAIL_REC gains beyond what either series would predict alone, because commuters combine workplace trips with retail stops; when both series move upward together the compounding effect pushes RETAIL_REC higher over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improved from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days even when WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both increase in the same week relative to the prior week.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility declined in the most recent week (-29.3 vs recent peak -26.0) after earlier recovery, consistent with early seasonal cooling reducing outdoor recreation substitution; as outdoor options shrink, some of that demand shifts back into indoor retail and recreation, modestly lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS peaked at -26.0 in t-3w then declined to -29.3 by t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next two weeks even as PARKS continues to decline week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility drops more than 4 points in a single week (suggesting a renewed restriction or closure order), this policy-driven signal will cause a compounding decline in RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks as broader activity restrictions take hold.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 4 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fluctuated between -55.6 and -52.6 over the snapshot with no large single-week drop yet
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or remains flat over the next 28 days despite a single-week WORKPLACES decline exceeding 4 points.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has stayed relatively stable and close to baseline recovery (around -28 to -31), indicating essential-trip behavior is saturated; because essential trips are decoupled from discretionary retail recovery, GROCERY_PHARM stability alone provides no directional signal and RETAIL_REC movement will track independently of it over the next four weeks, but should still trend upward given other activity signals.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM ranged narrowly between -31.4 and -28.4 across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC and GROCERY_PHARM move in the same direction with correlation above 0.7 over the next 28 days, implying coupling rather than independence.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, simultaneous week-on-week improvement in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES combined with a RESIDENTIAL decline signals an accelerating return to pre-pandemic routines; this triple interaction produces a stronger and faster RETAIL_REC increase within one week than any single series alone would predict.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise while RESIDENTIAL falls in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rose from t-1w to t-0w while RESIDENTIAL rose slightly
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within the next week even when TRANSIT and WORKPLACES jointly rise and RESIDENTIAL falls in the same week.
